statement: While a dispute is open on an Account, whoever started it (the Entity holds a record of the dispute it asked for, `starting`, or of the one the peer started, `against`, until the finalize, a lapse or the epoch move ends it), the node signs nothing new on it. It proposes no frame (its queue waits), and every frame its peer proposes is refused with the fault `frozen`, which can pass: the proposer takes the frame back and tries again once its view of J moves, so the payment commits in the epoch that follows or is refused then by the Account's own door. The one predicate that says so, `quiet` (the node's signature is out on a settlement or a C2R, R-COSIGN-FREEZE, or a dispute is open), feeds both the proposing and the rules the Account judges the peer's frames by. A command that takes on value (`pay`, `lock`, `offer`, `fill`) asked on an Account in dispute is refused back to whoever asked, with a `command_refused` notice and the fault `account_disputed`, so it is never queued to be zeroed by the rebase; a lock the paybook forwards into it fails back along the route as a refused entry does. When a dispute finalize moves the epoch on, the proof it paid by is named by the hash of its body, which the chain logs in `DisputeFinalized` (`finalProofbodyHash`, Depository.sol 142-148) and the watcher carries on the epoch event, and not by the nonce the chain stores: a timeout stores the opening nonce plus one but a finalize with a signed proof stores that proof's own nonce, and the two cannot be told apart from the logs (Depository.sol 962-976). The node takes the nonce of the proof it can name with that hash: the counter the chain registered against its own start, the proof the peer's dispute opened with, its committed state or the state its pending frame would commit (a dispute it started opened with its committed state, and its own counter was built from it; the freeze commits nothing after either). A hash no proof it can name has leaves the finalized nonce unknown, and the notices say so rather than guess. A node whose committed head is above that proof, or whose proof is unknown, (a frame the proof does not hold, committed after it was signed or sealed before the dispute and acked after it) is told, per token, to its owner (`offdelta_rebased`: peer, token, epoch, the committed nonce, the offdelta the node counted and the finalized nonce), so the node that counted a payment the rebase zeroes is told of it. A head at or below a known finalized nonce lost nothing and is told nothing, whatever its offdelta; a settlement or a C2R moving the epoch tells nothing (the chain reverts both while a dispute is open, and a settlement folds the offdelta into ondelta). The proposer of such a frame is told too: its ack is ignored during the dispute, so the frame stays pending with a committed nonce below the finalized one, and a node whose pending frame, above the finalized nonce (or with it unknown), carries a payment, a lock, an offer or a fill when a finalize moves the epoch is told which (`pending_rebased`: peer, epoch, the frame's nonce, the finalized nonce, the txs that spend and `fate`). A frame that carries only releases or a resolve, a pending frame at or below the finalized nonce, and one held by the proof the chain paid by, are told nothing. If the peer committed the frame before it heard of the dispute, the rebase zeroed what it paid; if it never heard of it, the peer refuses it as another epoch's: either way the frame stays pending and is sent again in the new epoch, where it commits or comes back as `tx_refused` (`fate` is `resent_in_new_epoch`), so the owner waits for that and does not ask again. The offdelta the finalized proof holds is not in either notice: the node that lost something did not open with that proof and holds none of its body (owed: read it from the start's or the counter's calldata; the DisputeFinalized event carries only the opening nonce and two hashes, Depository.sol 142-148). A frame of the node's own that was sealed before the dispute is not sent again while the dispute is open, and the ack of it commits nothing: it stays pending and is rebased with the epoch like any pending frame. A finalize settled every clause of its proof, so the holds are dissolved (R-HOLD-DISSOLVE) and a release queued for one is refused with a notice, never applied again in the epoch that follows. A payee behind a dispute cannot resolve in a frame, so the secret reaches the hub that forwarded the lock another way: every hosted Entity hears the chain's `SecretRevealed` as `j_secret` (at the configured depth, R-WATCH-READS-ALL) and the paybook passes the secret up for a lock it forwarded under that hash, on any Account, frozen or not; a resolve in a frame the node refuses as frozen shows its secret the same way, since a secret proves itself by its hash. A release (`resolve`, `cancel`, `expire`, `retract`, `lapse`) and `set_credit` wait in the queue for the new epoch. The proof the dispute rests on therefore stays the newest the node holds, and no frame is committed between the chain's finalize and the Entity hearing of it, because the Entity stays quiet until it hears the epoch move. Not here: a frame the peer sealed before it heard of the dispute and that this node acked before it heard of it (the peer commits it, this node's finalize or counter may not hold it; the notices say what the node counted and which nonce the chain paid by, not what the finalized proof held: owed, the offdelta of the finalized proof from calldata), the Host telling the Entity the epoch before it signs anything, the exact tokens a finalize pays (zeroing the union only understates, never overstates: owed, the Host reads the Account's holdings after the finalizing block), and the starter that never finalizes (owed, the next PR).
source: coordinator 10-02 11:55 (decision after the re-audit of PR 159)

R-DISPUTE-FREEZE a dispute the Host dropped, because its start would revert, ends it too

R-DISPUTE-FREEZE a release or a credit limit is not refused for the dispute, and nothing is sealed
R-DISPUTE-FREEZE once the dispute is over the payment is taken again
R-DISPUTE-FREEZE both sides' payments are refused with a notice and no frame goes out
R-DISPUTE-FREEZE after the finalize the Account is as the chain left it, without the refused payment
R-DISPUTE-FREEZE a frame a peer sealed before it heard of the dispute is refused as frozen
